content.body:
The Churchill was one of the most widely used British tanks of the war with dozens of variants employed in all theaters. Heavy armor virtually the equal of the German Tiger tank in many respects, coupled with a low silhouette made it a popular tank with its crews due to its survivability under fire. But its slow road speed and 6 pounder gun were key weaknesses. In its defense, it was one of the most unbeatable tanks of the war off road, due to its ability to climb steep grades.
The Churchill should be played like a bigger, badder, better Matilda II. You should remain cautious about air attacks because while your heavy armor all around will give you considerable security when you encounter enemy tanks, they will very likely call in heavy air support to eliminate you. This is something you should count on all the time; and if you are wrong, then all the better for you when you RTB.
The main threats you need to consider are the ubiquitous 88 mm FlaK gun, and the Tiger tank which mounts virtually the same weapon in an extremely heavily armored turret. Even though the Tiger usually enters the game world after the Churchill III does, the long 75 mm guns of the Panzer IV G and StuG III G can still put a hurt on the Churchill under the right circumstances. Your lack of speed will make flanking maneuver tactics difficult. It will always serve you better to use your low profile to act as an extremely nasty ambush tank; your armor allowing you to retreat or even advance under what could be very heavy enemy fire once they know where you are hiding. Try to keep a berm or terrain elevation between your tank and enemy fire as your tracks are as vulnerable as any tracked vehicle's.
The Churchill III will be a prime target for enemy forces be they tanks, bombers, AT guns or even anti-tank infantry. You must always assume you are the number one enemy target. The 6 pdr gun is a good AT gun, firing a high velocity if somewhat light AP round. The Crusader III is armed with exactly the same gun, but, being lighter and faster, can make a good running partner doing the flanking work while the Churchill slugs it out at in the more direct approach. The Churchill has good armor but its opponents have great guns in their 75's, frontal slugfests are best left to the dead tankers that they will soon become.
